title: Coffee against lemon juice
hook: Coffee is about pH 5, lemon juice about pH 2. How many times more hydrogen ions does lemon juice have?

knows: that acids are sour and pH measures acidity
that lower pH means more acidic
doesNotKnow: that pH is defined from hydrogen-ion concentration

misconception: pH is an ordinary linear scale, so pH 2 is a little more than twice as acidic as pH 5 (or 'three units more').
objective: The learner can explain that each step down in pH means 10 times more hydrogen ions, so three steps is 10 x 10 x 10 = 1,000 times, and a step up means one tenth.

claims.text: pH is minus the base-10 logarithm of the hydrogen-ion concentration (strictly, its activity), so one pH unit is a factor of 10.
claims.source: IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology (Gold Book), entry 'pH'; Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry. In dilute solutions activity is close to concentration.

claims.text: Going 3 pH units lower means 1,000 times more hydrogen ions in the same volume; going 2 units higher means 1/100 as many.
Lemon juice is roughly pH 2 (measured values run about 2.0 to 2.6).
claims.source: USGS Water Science School, 'pH and Water' (pH scale of common substances lists lemon juice near 2); FDA/CFSAN 'Approximate pH of Foods and Food Products' lists lemon juice 2.00-2.60.

claims.text: Black coffee is roughly pH 5 (typical brewed coffee is about 4.8 to 5.1).
claims.source: USGS Water Science School, 'pH and Water' (black coffee near 5); Rao & Fuller, Scientific Reports 8 (2018) 16030, measured hot and cold brew coffee at about pH 4.85-5.13.

claims.text: Pure water is pH 7 at 25 C.
claims.source: Kw = 1.0 x 10^-14 at 25 C, so [H+] = [OH-] = 10^-7 mol/L. Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry; CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics (ion product of water).

claims.text: From pH 0 to pH 14 the hydrogen-ion concentration changes by a factor of 10^14, one hundred trillion.
claims.source: 10^(14) = 100,000,000,000,000 (arithmetic from the definition of pH). v2: the sentence was removed from the reveal (learner finding 4: pH 0 and 14 never appear on the stage); no learner-visible text depends on this claim now. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Confirmed withdrawn: no 10^14 / pH 0-14 sentence on the stage or reveal (grep of Demo.tsx). Arithmetic 10^14 is right anyway.

claims.text: If black coffee is taken as pH 5 and lemon juice as pH 2 (round values), same-sized cups differ by exactly 1,000 times in hydrogen ions.
claims.source: From c2 with the round values: 10^(5-2) = 1,000. With the measured ranges in c3 and c4 the ratio runs from 10^(4.85-2.6) = 178 to 10^(5.13-2.0) = 1,349 (fact-checker, artifacts/scratch/fc2-ph-log-scale.mjs). v2 frames the predict question and reveal as round values (fact-check F1). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 13): 10^(5-2) = 1,000 exactly for the round values; framing as round values is in the reveal (Demo.tsx TARGET_TIMES, "is exactly 1,000"). Pass-2 range check stands.

claims.text: A lower pH means more hydrogen ions in the same volume, and a more acidic solution.
claims.source: From c1: pH = -log10[H+], so [H+] = 10^(-pH) rises as pH falls; acidity in the pH sense is the hydrogen-ion activity (IUPAC Gold Book, 'pH'). Stage caption v2 "Lower pH, more ions." and slider label "slide right for more acid" (learner finding 3).

recall.question: A liquid at pH 4 versus pure water at pH 7: how many times more hydrogen ions does the pH 4 liquid have?
recall.why: Each pH step is a factor of 10, and 7 - 4 = 3 steps: 10 x 10 x 10 = 1,000.
